title: Short-exact devissage for the eight assertions
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure], let $C$ be a separated scheme of finite type over $k$ with $\dim C\le1$, and let

$$
 0\longrightarrow F_1\xrightarrow{\ \alpha\ }F\xrightarrow{\ \beta\ }F_2\longrightarrow0
$$

be a short exact sequence in the abelian category $\Ab(C_{\Et})$ of abelian sheaves on the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves] in which $F_1$ and $F_2$ are torsion [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], so that $(C,F_1)$ and $(C,F_2)$ are curve coefficient pairs [def-weil-pbc-curve-setting]. Then $F$ is torsion, so $(C,F)$ is a curve coefficient pair. For a curve coefficient pair $(C,G)$ read each of the eight assertions $\mathcal C_j(C,G)$ of [def-weil-pbc-eight-curve-assertions] as an implication about this pair: its conclusion is asserted whenever its hypotheses (on $C$, on $\operatorname{char}k$, on $G$, and for every algebraically closed extension $k'/k$, every open immersion $a:U\hookrightarrow C$ and every degree $q$ in its range) are met, and it holds when they fail (Stacks, Situation 0A52). If $\mathcal C(C,F_1)$ and $\mathcal C(C,F_2)$ hold, then $\mathcal C(C,F)$ holds. In particular the class of torsion abelian sheaves $G$ on $C_{\Et}$ with $\mathcal C(C,G)$ is closed under extensions.

proof.text: Forget the module structure in the short exact sequence. Underlying abelian sheaves preserve kernels; sheaf epimorphisms are locally surjective and remain so after forgetting scalars. The existing theorem `AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.shortExact_map_forget₂` supplies the short exact abelian sequence A. Map monomorphisms and epimorphisms through geometric stalk functors: the first stalk is a submodule and the third is a quotient of the middle stalk. Thus primary torsion and torsion of invertible order pass to both outer terms, proved by primary_outer and invertible_outer. For constructibility use the general Noetherian-ring subsheaf lemma for the first term, then the source library's proved constructible cokernel theorem and the canonical short-exact cokernel isomorphism for the third; X is Noetherian because it is quasi-compact and locally of finite type over a field.

For C1-C3, install the applicable vanishing conclusions for the two outer terms. Ext covariant exactness at the middle group writes any middle class as the image of an outer class once its image on the right vanishes; both outer groups are zero. This is the complete helper subsingleton_middle. For C4-C5 use the same exact segment and finite_middle, applying ShortComplex.Exact.ab_finite to the Ext cohomology segment. These arguments are used at every degree required by the assertions.

For C6-C7 apply the existing natural long exact ladder to the actual pullback morphism of any cartesian square. The proved helper bijective_middle_cohomologyMap performs the diagram chase: lift an image in the third group, remove its boundary using injectivity in the next first group, then correct the residual difference through the first group. Injectivity uses surjectivity of the previous third-group map to remove a boundary. In degree zero it uses the initial injective map instead. The outer assertions supply bijectivity at all degrees. No assumption that k itself is algebraically closed is used by this conditional devissage.

For C8 the first outer assertion C1 kills H3 of the first term. In the natural ladder for an open immersion, lift the third image by its C8, lift it to the middle using this H3 vanishing, and correct the residual difference through the first term by its C8. This is the proved helper surjective_middle_cohomologyMap at q=2. Assemble all eight fields into the unchanged IsCurve.Assertions structure.

blueprint_sketch.statement:
Let

$$
0\longrightarrow F_1\xrightarrow{a}F\xrightarrow{b}F_2\longrightarrow0
$$

be exact. If all applicable assertions $\mathcal C_r(X,F_i)$ hold for
$i=1,2$, then all applicable assertions hold for $F$.
blueprint_sketch.proof:
Pullback to an extension field is exact, so the displayed sequence and its
base change give natural long exact cohomology sequences.

For (1), (2), and (3), in every degree above the stated bound the exact
segment

$$
H^q(X,F_1)\xrightarrow{a_*}H^q(X,F)
\xrightarrow{b_*}H^q(X,F_2)
$$

has zero end terms. Hence its middle term is zero. The hypotheses on
affineness and characteristic are unchanged, and in (3) an extension of two
$p$-power torsion sheaves is again killed by a power of $p$.

For (4) and (5), constructible sheaves form a Serre subcategory: on a common
finite stratification the stalk sequence is an exact sequence of finite
groups. Prime-to-characteristic torsion is also preserved by extensions.
Exactness identifies $H^q(X,F)$ as an extension of
$\operatorname{im}a_*$ by $\operatorname{im}b_*$; these are respectively a
quotient of the finite group $H^q(X,F_1)$ and a subgroup of the finite group
$H^q(X,F_2)$. Thus $H^q(X,F)$ is finite.

For (6) and (7), write the long exact sequence for $F_1,F,F_2$ above its
base-changed sequence. Every square commutes because restriction commutes
with $a$, $b$, and the boundary map obtained from an injective resolution.
For fixed $q$, the four outer vertical arrows in the five-term portion

$$
H^{q-1}(F_2)\to H^q(F_1)\to H^q(F)\to H^q(F_2)\to H^{q+1}(F_1)
$$

are isomorphisms; the five lemma makes the middle arrow an isomorphism.

For (8), let $c\in H^2(W,F|_W)$ and put $c_2=b_*(c)$. Choose
$x_2\in H^2(X,F_2)$ restricting to $c_2$. Its boundary lies in
$H^3(X,F_1)=0$ by (1), so exactness gives
$x\in H^2(X,F)$ with $b_*(x)=x_2$. The difference
$c-x|_W$ maps to zero in $H^2(W,F_2|_W)$, hence equals $a_*(d_1)$ for some
$d_1\in H^2(W,F_1|_W)$. Choose $y_1\in H^2(X,F_1)$ restricting to $d_1$.
Then $x+a_*(y_1)$ restricts to $c$. This proves the eighth assertion and
completes all eight cases compressed in Tag `0A5C`.

split_report.summary: Statement made precise (k algebraically closed, C separated of finite type of dimension <= 1, the sequence in Ab(C_et) with F_1, F_2 torsion in the sense of def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves as def-weil-pbc-curve-setting uses it; F torsion is now a conclusion; each C_j read as an implication about the pair, as the users do), checked against Stacks 0A5C (lemma-ses-statements) and its proof. Proof written in eight steps: F torsion (sectionwise kernel, composite coverings); the passage of the hypotheses of C3-C6 from F to F_1, F_2 (stalks exact for p-primary / prime to p; constructibility by the new node lem-weil-pbc-curve-constructible-sub-quotient, Stacks 09BH(2)), which the imported proof skipped; the long exact sequences and the pullback ladder from lem-weil-pbc-pullback-cohomology-long-exact-ladder (cited, not re-proved); C1-C3 by exactness with zero outer terms; C4-C5 by the new Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-finite-middle-of-exact (CategoryTheory.ShortComplex.Exact.ab_finite); C6-C7 by the ladder for u = pi and the five lemma in degrees q-1, q, q+1 with the q = 0 padding; C8 by the chase with the maps named (H^3(C,F_1) = 0 by C1, ladder for u = a, restriction = pullback by clause 5 of lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial). The slopmaster2 declaration AlgebraicGeometry.IsCurve.Assertions.of_shortExact (Curve/Reductions.lean 90-102, own sorry) states this lemma for sheaves of Lambda-modules; the node's lean_audit says none.
